name: Platform-Neutral Fallback Authentication Path Definition
consequences: Defining a platform-neutral fallback authentication path would provide an alternative to the current Apple/Google dependency, reducing Denmark's digital sovereignty risk. However, this lever introduces trade-offs in terms of integration complexity and potential vendor pushback.
options: Develop a FIDO2/WebAuthn-based fallback authentication system with GrapheneOS as the primary platform
Implement a browser-based fallback authentication path using OpenID Connect on multiple platforms
Establish a hardware-token-based fallback mechanism that reduces dependence on mobile OS duopoly
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the increased complexity in integrating a platform-neutral fallback authentication path, which may lead to vendor pushback and delayed adoption.

name: Digital Identity Standards Harmonization
consequences: Harmonizing digital identity standards would facilitate interoperability among Danish public sector identity providers and reduce the reliance on foreign technology suppliers. However, this lever introduces trade-offs in terms of regulatory compliance and potential vendor resistance.
options: Align Danish digital identity standards with EU's eIDAS and NSIS frameworks
Develop a custom standard for platform-neutral authentication protocols
Establish a national standard for secure authentication methods
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential resistance from vendors who may not comply with harmonized standards, leading to fragmentation in the market.

name: Procurement and Contractual Reforms
consequences: Implementing procurement and contractual reforms would enable the Danish government to specify platform-neutral requirements for digital identity systems. However, this lever introduces trade-offs in terms of regulatory compliance and potential vendor pushback.
options: Reform procurement processes to prioritize platform-neutrality and fallback access
Develop contractual clauses that enforce platform-neutral authentication protocols
Establish a national framework for secure authentication methods
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential resistance from vendors who may not comply with new procurement requirements, leading to increased regulatory complexity.

name: Coalition Building and Advocacy
consequences: Building a coalition and engaging in advocacy efforts would help raise awareness about Denmark's digital sovereignty risks and promote platform-neutral solutions. However, this lever introduces trade-offs in terms of coalition cohesion and potential vendor influence.
options: Build a coalition with civil society organizations, privacy advocates, and security experts
Engage in advocacy efforts to promote platform-neutral authentication protocols
Establish partnerships with EU bodies and technical working groups
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential fragmentation within the coalition due to differing interests and priorities.

Establish a hardware-token-based fallback mechanism
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential resistance from vendors who may not comply with new technical standards, leading to increased regulatory complexity.

options: Reform regulatory frameworks to prioritize platform-neutrality and fallback access
Develop policy guidelines that enforce platform-neutral authentication protocols
Establish a national framework for secure authentication methods
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential resistance from vendors who may not comply with new regulatory requirements, leading to increased complexity.

name: Physical Location Establishment
consequences: Establishing a physical location for research and development would enable the project team to engage with government bodies and stakeholders. However, this lever introduces trade-offs in terms of resource allocation and potential vendor influence.
options: Establish a physical base in Copenhagen for research and development
Secure access-controlled workspace for security-sensitive digital identity research
Develop partnerships with local universities and research institutions
review: The primary trade-off of this lever is the potential influence from vendors who may not comply with new regulations, leading to increased regulatory complexity.

name: Alternative Trust Anchor Framework Development
consequences: Developing an alternative trust anchor framework would allow Denmark to decouple its digital identity infrastructure from Apple and Google, reducing reliance on foreign technology suppliers.
options: Design a decentralized trust model using blockchain-based identities and cryptographic proofs of work
Implement a hybrid approach combining centralized platform integrity signals with decentralized identity verification
Establish an open-source trust anchor framework leveraging FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect standards
review: Introducing alternative trust anchors introduces trade-offs between security, scalability, and maintenance costs. The options leave unaddressed the challenge of achieving widespread adoption among existing digital identity stakeholders.

name: Public-Private Partnership for Digital Identity Infrastructure
consequences: Establishing a public-private partnership would enable Denmark to leverage private sector expertise and resources in developing its digital identity infrastructure, while ensuring alignment with national security and sovereignty requirements.
options: Create a joint venture between the government and a leading tech company to develop a platform-neutral eIDAS2 wallet
Establish a public-private working group to define standards for secure and resilient digital identity systems
Develop a crowdsourced funding model to support open-source development of digital identity infrastructure components
review: Forming a public-private partnership introduces trade-offs between control, accountability, and intellectual property rights. The options leave unaddressed the challenge of balancing competing interests among partners.

name: Digital Identity Infrastructure Consolidation
consequences: Consolidating Denmark's digital identity infrastructure would enable the country to simplify its architecture, reduce reliance on foreign technology suppliers, and enhance security.
options: Develop a unified eIDAS2 wallet platform integrating multiple existing identity providers
Establish a public-private working group to define standards for secure and resilient digital identity systems
Create an open-source framework for developing and implementing standardized digital identity components
review: Consolidating the digital identity infrastructure introduces trade-offs between security, scalability, and maintenance costs. The options leave unaddressed the challenge of achieving widespread adoption among existing digital identity stakeholders.

name: Digital Identity Infrastructure Upgrade
consequences: Upgrading Denmark's digital identity infrastructure would enable the country to leverage new technologies, reduce reliance on foreign technology suppliers, and enhance security.
options: Implement a blockchain-based identity management system for secure and resilient digital identity
Develop an open-source framework for developing and implementing standardized digital identity components
Establish a public-private working group to define standards for secure and resilient digital identity systems
review: Upgrading the digital identity infrastructure introduces trade-offs between security, scalability, and maintenance costs. The options leave unaddressed the challenge of achieving widespread adoption among existing digital identity stakeholders.

name: Influencing Digitaliseringsstyrelsen's Procurement Strategy
consequences: Redirecting procurement towards standards-compliant vendors reduces platform lock-in, but it may also delay or increase the cost of AltID rollout.
options: Implement a tiered procurement system with separate tracks for standards-compliant and proprietary solutions
Develop a public-private partnership model that incentivizes vendor compliance with Denmark's digital identity standards
Create a government-led procurement framework that prioritizes platform-neutrality and fallback access
review: Changing AltID procurement strategy alone does not address the need for a certified fallback authentication path, which remains a technical challenge.

name: Establishing an Industry-Led Standards Body
consequences: A standards body can drive convergence towards platform-neutral solutions, but it may also create new dependencies and power imbalances within the industry.
options: Form a coalition of Danish companies to develop and promote open standards for digital identity
Establish an independent, government-recognized standards body that sets interoperability requirements for AltID and related services
Create a public-private partnership to develop and certify platform-neutral authentication protocols
review: While a standards body can drive convergence towards platform-neutral solutions, it may also create new dependencies and power imbalances within the industry.

name: Developing an Open-Source Fallback Authentication Framework
consequences: An open-source fallback framework can provide a platform-neutral access path, but it may also require significant community engagement and maintenance efforts.
options: Develop a publicly funded, open-source fallback authentication framework that uses standards-compliant protocols
Create a collaborative development environment where industry stakeholders contribute to an open-source fallback framework
Establish a government-led initiative to develop and certify an open-source fallback authentication protocol
review: While an open-source fallback framework can provide a platform-neutral access path, it may also require significant community engagement and maintenance efforts.

name: Influencing EU Digital Identity Wallet Framework
consequences: Aligning Denmark's advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in can drive convergence towards platform-neutral solutions.
options: Engage with relevant EU bodies to promote language in European Digital Identity Wallet materials that supports platform-neutral access or certified fallback mechanisms
Collaborate with other EU member states to develop a joint position on platform-neutrality and fallback access within the European Digital Identity Wallet framework
Establish an industry-led initiative to drive convergence towards platform-neutral solutions across Europe
review: While influencing the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework can drive convergence towards platform-neutral solutions, it may also require significant coordination and negotiation efforts.

name: Developing a National Digital Identity Strategy
consequences: A national digital identity strategy can provide a clear roadmap for reducing dependency on foreign technology suppliers and establishing a platform-neutral fallback authentication path.
options: Develop a comprehensive national digital identity strategy that prioritizes platform-neutrality and fallback access
Create a government-led initiative to develop and certify a national digital identity framework that supports platform-neutral solutions
Establish an industry-led coalition to promote the development of a national digital identity strategy that prioritizes platform-neutrality
review: While developing a national digital identity strategy can provide a clear roadmap, it may also require significant coordination and negotiation efforts.
